introduction_section.heading: What is
content: Performance testing is the process of putting your application under simulated real-world stress to see exactly how it behaves, where it bottlenecks, and at what point it completely breaks. It answers the critical question: 'Will our servers survive if our marketing campaign goes viral?' [Image of a performance load testing graph showing virtual users scaling up versus application response time and server CPU load]

At Devisgon, we simulate thousands of concurrent users hitting your APIs, databases, and web servers simultaneously. By identifying memory leaks, slow database queries, and inadequate server resources before your big launch, we ensure your application never leaves your customers staring at a loading screen.
introduction_section.highlight_quote: “In the digital world, slow is just another word for broken.”

process_section.title: Our Process
process_section.subtitle: A scientific approach to application speed

steps.title: Baseline Analysis
steps.description: We define your Service Level Agreements (SLAs), target response times, and expected user load.

steps.title: Scenario Scripting
steps.description: We write custom scripts that mimic realistic user behaviors (e.g., searching, adding to cart, and checking out).

steps.title: Execution
steps.description: We deploy virtual users from multiple geographic locations to bombard your servers with traffic.

steps.title: Analyze & Optimize
steps.description: We isolate the exact layer (frontend, API, or database) causing delays and help your team tune the performance.

case_study_section.headline: Ensuring a ticketing platform could handle 100,000 fans in 5 minutes

problem.label: Problem
problem.text: An event ticketing platform was preparing to launch a highly anticipated music festival but had crashed during smaller sales in the past due to database deadlocks.

solution.label: Solution
solution.text: We designed a spike test using distributed cloud servers to simulate 100,000 users attempting to buy tickets simultaneously, uncovering critical bottlenecks in their payment gateway API and Redis cache.

result.label: Result
result.text: After applying our tuning recommendations, the platform successfully processed the entire 100,000-user rush with a 100% uptime and average response times under 2 seconds.

faq_section.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq_section.subtitle: Get answers about performance and load testing

questions.question: What is the difference between Load Testing and Stress Testing?
questions.answer: Load testing checks how your system handles the *expected* amount of normal traffic. Stress testing pushes the system far beyond the expected traffic to intentionally break it, helping us understand its absolute maximum capacity and failure behavior.

questions.question: Will performance testing crash our live website?
questions.answer: It can, which is why we rarely execute heavy load tests on a live production server! We prefer to run these tests on a staging environment that perfectly mirrors your production hardware, ensuring your actual users are never interrupted.

questions.question: What metrics do you track during a test?
questions.answer: We track a wide variety of metrics, including Average Response Time, Error Rates (like 500 or 502 gateway errors), Throughput (requests per second), CPU utilization, memory consumption, and network I/O.

questions.question: How long does a performance testing engagement take?
questions.answer: Setting up the infrastructure, writing the complex user-journey scripts, and executing the initial rounds of testing typically takes between 1 to 3 weeks, depending on the complexity of the application flows we need to simulate.
